direction: Develop an exact (non-approximate) joint-training solver that differentiates through RoI pooling with respect to predicted box coordinates, using an RoI warping layer.
quote: a solution can be given by an “RoI warping” layer as developed in [15], which is beyond the scope of this paper.
realizationNote: Realized by OD014 (Mask R-CNN) whose quantization-free RoIAlign layer differentiably resamples RoIs with respect to box coordinates, supplying exactly the RoI-warping joint training Faster R-CNN left as future work.

direction: Reduce the feature stride (e.g. by predicting on finer-resolution maps) to gain further detection accuracy.
quote: accuracy may be further improved with a smaller stride.
realizationNote: Realized by OD010 (FPN) which predicts on much finer stride-4 maps across a feature pyramid, capturing the accuracy gains Faster R-CNN anticipated.

direction: Release DenseBox2, a real-time version of the detector for KITTI car detection and face detection.
quote: We will present another paper describing a real-time detection system on KITTI and face detection, called DenseBox2.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper released a DenseBox2 real-time detector for KITTI or face detection, so this direction remains unimplemented.

direction: Extend landmark supervision to car detection (the paper manually annotates keypoints for KITTI and plans to release them).
quote: we manually annotate a set of keypoints for the KITTI car detection dataset [13] and will release annotation afterward.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper released KITTI car keypoint annotations or reused landmark-style supervision to improve car detection.

direction: Combine SSD with recurrent neural networks to detect and track objects in video simultaneously.
quote: A promising future direction is to explore its use as part of a system using recurrent neural networks to detect and track objects in video simultaneously.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD017 (RRC) which brought recurrent rolling convolution into single-image detection, but the detect-and-track-in-video combination was never built.

direction: Design a better default-box tiling aligned with each position's receptive field.
quote: An alternative way of improving SSD is to design a better tiling of default boxes so that its position and scale are better aligned with the receptive field of each position on a feature map. We leave this for future work.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD011 (k-means anchor priors), OD035 (MetaAnchor generation) and OD044 (Guided Anchoring), which redesigned anchor tiling substantially, though exact receptive-field alignment was never achieved.

direction: Use a faster base network so that the larger SSD512 model can also run in real time.
quote: using a faster base network could even further improve the speed, which can possibly make the SSD512 model real-time as well.
realizationNote: Realized by OD016 (MobileNets) and OD031 (MobileNetV2) which supplied efficient base networks enabling large SSD-style detectors to run in real time.

direction: Adopt orthogonal FCN extensions developed for semantic segmentation and further region-based detection extensions, which the simple R-FCN system should absorb without difficulty.
quote: There have been a series of orthogonal extensions of FCNs that were developed for semantic segmentation (e.g., see [2]), as well as extensions of region-based methods for object detection (e.g., see [9, 1, 22]).
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD014 (Mask R-CNN) and OD023 (Light-Head R-CNN) which pushed the region-based FCN line forward by absorbing FPN, RoIAlign and light heads, though R-FCN itself was not extended point-for-point.

direction: Extend IoU loss and UnitBox beyond face detection to other object localization and detection tasks.
quote: We believe that the IoU loss layer as well as the UnitBox will be of great value to other object localization and detection tasks.
realizationNote: Realized by OD046 (FCOS) and OD056 (YOLOv4) which carried IoU-based box losses into general detection, with CIoU becoming a standard component far beyond face detection.

direction: Apply the thin-but-deep design principle to other vision tasks such as face recognition and semantic analysis.
quote: we believe that our design principle is widely applicable to other tasks such as face recognition and semantic analysis.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD016 (MobileNets) and OD031 (MobileNetV2) which applied the fewer-channels-more-layers principle to detection backbones, but not to face recognition or semantic analysis.

direction: Combine the architecture with network compression and quantization techniques for further real-world speedups.
quote: All kinds of recent compression and quantization techniques are applicable to our network as well to further increase the actual performance in real applications.
realizationNote: Realized by OD091 (YOLOv6) which shipped quantization- and pruning-based compression for an efficient detection network, validating the combination on real-world speedups.

direction: Integrate complementary efficient detection structures (R-FCN, SSD) with PVANet.
quote: their methodologies can be easily integrated with PVAN ET and further reduce its computational cost.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD023 (Light-Head R-CNN) which coupled a tiny backbone with an R-FCN-style efficient head, and by OD045 (ThunderNet), though PVANet itself was not reused.

direction: Finish running and fold in the high-resolution SSD configurations that had not yet converged at submission time.
quote: models for a small subset of experimental configurations (namely some of the high resolution SSD models) have yet to converge, so we have for now omitted them from analysis.
realizationNote: The paper's own unfinished high-resolution SSD runs were never completed or reported by any later corpus paper.

direction: Combine FPN with complementary accuracy improvements such as iterative regression, hard negative mining, context modeling and stronger data augmentation.
quote: These improvements are complementary to FPNs and should boost accuracy further.
realizationNote: Realized by OD020 (RetinaNet) and OD029 (Cascade R-CNN) which paired FPN with focal loss, hard-example focus and iterative regression, exactly the complementary boosts FPN anticipated.

direction: Adopt stronger head architectures on top of the feature pyramid.
quote: We expect a stronger architecture of the head [30] will improve upon our results, which is beyond the focus of this paper.
realizationNote: Realized by OD048 (Double-Head) which replaced the plain pyramid head with separate conv/fc heads on top of the feature pyramid after an explicit head-analysis.

direction: Use FPN as a practical building block for future detection research and applications.
quote: We believe the efficiency and simplicity of our method will benefit future research and applications.
realizationNote: Realized by OD014 (Mask R-CNN) and OD020 (RetinaNet) which adopted FPN as the standard feature-pyramid building block for region- and dense-detection research.

direction: Apply the joint weakly-supervised technique to image segmentation.
quote: For future work we hope to use similar techniques for weakly supervised image segmentation.
realizationNote: Weakly supervised segmentation via the joint detection/classification training scheme was not pursued in any later corpus paper.

direction: Improve detection by using stronger strategies for assigning weak labels to classification images during training.
quote: We also plan to improve our detection results using more powerful matching strategies for assigning weak labels to classification data during training.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD081 (GLIP) and OD097 (self-training) which scaled weakly/pseudo-labeled data into detection training, though image-level classification-label matching itself was not strengthened.

direction: Use hierarchical classification for dataset combination in classification and segmentation.
quote: Dataset combination using hierarchical classification would be useful in the classification and segmentation domains.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper combined datasets via hierarchical classification for classification or segmentation.

direction: Bring different sources and structures of data together to build stronger visual models.
quote: We will continue looking for ways to bring different sources and structures of data together to make stronger models of the visual world.
realizationNote: Realized by OD081 (GLIP) and OD111 (DINO-X) which merged detection, grounding and large weakly-labeled image sets into stronger multi-source visual models.

direction: Find better functions for combining encoder and decoder features beyond the element-wise product.
quote: The better feature combination can be considered as further work to improve the accuracy of the DSSD model.
realizationNote: Realized by OD053 (EfficientDet/BiFPN) which replaced fixed element-wise combination with learned online weighted feature fusion, and by OD033 (PANet) with an alternative fusion path.

direction: Speed up DSSD by replacing the learned deconvolution layer with simple bilinear up-sampling.
quote: A potential way to speed up DSSD is to replace the deconvolution layer by a simple bilinear up-sampling.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD053 (BiFPN) which substituted cheap resampling for learned deconvolution in its neck, though DSSD's deconvolution was never directly replaced with bilinear up-sampling.

direction: Extend the encoder-decoder hourglass approach beyond SSD to region-based detectors.
quote: this approach can be applied to other detection methods, such as the R-CNN series methods [12, 11, 24], as well.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD033 (PANet) which carried top-down decoder-style pyramids into region-based Mask R-CNN detection, though not the DSSD deconvolution hourglass specifically.

direction: Improve the efficiency and effectiveness of encoder-decoder feature combination.
quote: we expect many improvements in finding more efficient and effective ways to combine the features from the encoder and decoder
realizationNote: Realized by OD033 (PANet) and OD053 (BiFPN) which steadily made encoder-decoder feature combination both more efficient and more effective.

direction: Extend deformable RoI pooling to pooling regions of multiple sizes as in spatial pyramid pooling.
quote: While the regions are of the same size currently, extension to multiple sizes as in spatial pyramid pooling [34] is straightforward.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper extended deformable RoI pooling to multi-size spatial-pyramid pooling.

direction: Extend the deformable modules beyond 2D to 3D feature maps.
quote: Extension to 3D is straightforward.
realizationNote: Deformable convolution and RoI pooling were never extended to 3D feature maps in the corpus.

direction: Combine the instance-first and segmentation-first strategies more deeply.
quote: We expect a deeper incorporation of both strategies will be studied in the future.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD057 (DETR) and OD072 (QueryInst) which unified detection with segmentation and instance-level tasks, though the specific instance-first/segmentation-first blend was not literally built.

direction: Explore more complex mask branch designs.
quote: More complex designs have the potential to improve performance but are not the focus of this work.
realizationNote: Realized by OD033 (PANet) which added adaptive pooling and a complementary fc mask branch, and by OD072 (QueryInst) which introduced dynamic mask heads.

direction: Pursue better speed/accuracy trade-offs by varying image sizes and proposal numbers.
quote: better speed/accuracy tradeoffs could be achieved [21], e.g., by varying image sizes and proposal numbers, which is beyond the scope of this paper.
realizationNote: Realized by OD053 (EfficientDet) which explored speed/accuracy trade-offs by systematically scaling input resolution and network capacity, and by OD045 (ThunderNet) for edge settings.

direction: Apply the framework to other instance-level recognition tasks.
quote: Given the effectiveness of Mask R-CNN for extracting object bounding boxes, masks, and keypoints, we expect it be an effective framework for other instance-level tasks.
realizationNote: Realized by OD072 (QueryInst) for instance segmentation and by OD111 (DINO-X) which extended the Mask R-CNN-style framework to boxes, masks and keypoints with multiple heads.

direction: Explore other re-scoring functions beyond linear and Gaussian, such as generalized logistic functions like Gompertz, accepting more hyper-parameters.
quote: Apart from the two proposed functions, other functions with more parameters can also be explored with Soft-NMS which take overlap and detection scores into account.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD059 (score voting) and OD061 (Matrix NMS) which introduced alternative post-processing re-scoring beyond linear/Gaussian, but generalized-logistic softness was never adopted.

direction: Try generalized logistic (e.g. Gompertz) weighting functions for Soft-NMS.
quote: For example, instances of the generalized logistic function like the Gompertz function can be used, but such functions would increase the number of hyper-parameters.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper adopted Gompertz or generalized-logistic re-scoring for Soft-NMS.

direction: Release pre-trained MobileNet models in TensorFlow to aid adoption and exploration.
quote: As a next step to help adoption and exploration of MobileNets, we plan on releasing models in Tensor Flow.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper documents releasing TensorFlow MobileNet checkpoints or discusses model release for adoption.

direction: Design an efficient memory mechanism for detection.
quote: We leave the design of an efficient memory mechanism for detection to our future work.
realizationNote: An efficient memory mechanism for detection was never designed in the corpus.

direction: Investigate memory-enabled recurrent architectures for object detection and quantify their impact.
quote: In the future work, we planned to investigate the memory enabled recurrent architecture in the context of object detection and quantify its impact to the detection performance.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper built or quantified a memory-enabled recurrent architecture for detection.

direction: Generalize RRC to 3D object detection and related applications.
quote: We are also interested in generalizing RRC to the task of 3D object detection and related applications.
realizationNote: Recurrent rolling convolution was not generalized to 3D object detection or related applications.

direction: Apply the Resblock + unified prediction design beyond SSD to other architectures that use multi-scale features.
quote: We expect the proposed method be not restricted to SSD-based methods but also applicable to other structures utilizing multi-scale features.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD033 (PANet) and OD053 (BiFPN) which applied residual-block-based features to multi-scale architectures pervasively, though RUN's unified-prediction head was not adopted.

direction: Apply from-scratch training to non-RGB domains (depth, medical, multi-spectral imagery) where ImageNet pre-training does not transfer.
quote: Our future work will consider these domains, as well as learning ultra efficient DSOD models to support resource-bounded devices.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD040 which made from-scratch training viable for strong detectors and by OD077 which worked in a non-RGB thermal domain, but depth/medical/multi-spectral from-scratch was not demonstrated.

direction: Clarify whether pre-training the DSOD backbone on ImageNet helps or not, which the single probe left open.
quote: Future work will investigate this point more thoroughly.
realizationNote: Realized by OD040 (Rethinking ImageNet Pre-training) which showed that with proper normalization and schedule from-scratch training matches ImageNet pre-training, settling DSOD's open probe for strong detectors.

direction: Design specialized architectures to operate in the very high frame-rate regime, which this work explicitly leaves open.
quote: Addressing the high frame rate regime will likely require special network design, as in [27], and is beyond the scope of this work.
realizationNote: Realized by OD045 (ThunderNet) and OD091 (YOLOv6) which designed specialized, deployment-targeted architectures for the high-frame-rate regime.

direction: Generalize beyond the exact focal loss formula to any loss with similar down-weighting properties (as explored with FL* in the appendix).
quote: The exact form of the focal loss is not crucial.
realizationNote: Realized by OD058 (Generalized Focal Loss) and OD062 (Varifocal Loss) which generalized the down-weighting idea beyond focal loss's exact exponential form.

direction: Adopt the stronger ResNeXt-101-FPN backbone reported after the main results to push accuracy further past 40 AP.
quote: Plugging in ResNeXt32x8d-101-FPN [38] as the RetinaNet backbone further improves results another 1.7 AP, surpassing 40 AP on COCO.
realizationNote: Realized by OD053 (EfficientDet) whose scaled backbones pushed COCO AP well past 40, fulfilling the stronger-backbone route for FPN detectors.

direction: Apply RefineDet to specific object categories such as pedestrians, vehicles and faces, and add an attention mechanism.
quote: In the future, we plan to employ RefineDet to detect some other specific kinds of objects, e.g., pedestrian, vehicle, and face, and introduce the attention mechanism in RefineDet to further improve the performance.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD047 (Gaussian YOLOv3) for vehicle-focused autonomous-driving detection and OD052 (ASSD) adding attention to a one-stage detector, though RefineDet itself was not extended.

direction: Train with larger input images than 320x320/512x512 to raise accuracy once resources allow.
quote: We believe the accuracy of RefineDet can be further improved using larger input images.
realizationNote: Realized by OD053 (scaled input resolutions) and OD071 (PP-YOLOv2 at 640/768) which confirmed that larger training images raise detection accuracy.

direction: Combine focal loss with RefineDet, since the authors view it as complementary to their design.
quote: We believe that it can be used in RefineNet to further improve the performance.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD046 (FCOS) and OD044 (Guided Anchoring) which combined focal loss with dense one-stage detectors, but the specifically proposed RefineDet combination was not explored.

direction: Understand why large-mini-batch epoch-wise accuracy curves differ from those in image classification.
quote: We leave the understanding of this phenomenon as the future work.
realizationNote: The cause of detection-specific epoch-wise accuracy curves under large mini-batches was not explained by later corpus work.

direction: Extend the variance-based interpretation of the learning rate to wider applications beyond detection.
quote: We hope the variance analysis here can shed light on deeper understanding of learning rate in wider applications.
realizationNote: The variance-based learning-rate interpretation was never extended beyond detection in the corpus.

direction: Use RoI-align instead of the current pooling scheme for further accuracy gains in the fast setting.
quote: Noticing that it will obtain better results if we involve RoI-align.
realizationNote: Realized by OD033 (PANet) and OD048 (Double-Head) which made RoIAlign-style alignment the default pooling for region-based detectors, confirming the expected accuracy gain.

direction: Apply the repulsion loss to other object detection tasks beyond pedestrian detection.
quote: We expect wide application of the proposed loss in many other object detection tasks.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD056 (YOLOv4/CIoU) which expanded overlap-aware box losses beyond pedestrian detection, though repulsion loss itself was not re-applied to general detection.

direction: The VOC extension already points to using RepLoss in general (non-pedestrian) crowd-scene detection.
quote: These results demonstrate that our method is generic and can be extended to general object detection.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD057 (DETR) which attacked general crowded-scene detection via set prediction, but RepLoss itself was never carried to non-pedestrian detection.

direction: Extend RFB to more lightweight backbones and target deployment on low-end devices.
quote: This suggests its great potential for applications on low-end devices.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD045 (ThunderNet) and OD053 (EfficientDet) which fielded efficient detectors for low-end devices, though RFB was not transplanted onto lightweight backbones.

direction: Pursue efficient accuracy gains such as fusing up-sampled conv7_fc features with conv4_3 and widening RFB branches, rather than increasing input resolution.
quote: On the other hand, we can see that RFB Net500 averagely consumes 30 ms per image, while RetinaNet needs 90 ms.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD053 whose weighted fusion rebalanced efficiency and accuracy without simply raising input resolution, while RFB's specific conv7_fc/conv4_3 fusion was not pursued.

direction: Skip back-propagation for large objects in high-resolution images to cut computation, which the authors flag as future work.
quote: We would like to explore this direction in future work.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper skipped back-propagation for large objects in high-resolution images to cut computation.

direction: Combine features with predictions at multiple layers for a further boost.
quote: A more careful combination of features with predictions at multiple layers like [23, 13] should provide a further boost in performance.
realizationNote: Realized by OD033 (bottom-up path augmentation and adaptive pooling) and OD053 (BiFPN) which combined features and predictions across multiple layers.

direction: Plug SNIP into other tasks with large scale variation such as instance segmentation, pose estimation and spatio-temporal action detection.
quote: The proposed approach is generic and can be plugged into the training pipeline of different problems like instancesegmentation, pose-estimation, spatio-temporal action detection
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD043 (TridentNet) which continued scale-invariant detection design, but SNIP was not plugged into segmentation, pose or spatio-temporal detection.

direction: Integrate RBox into proposal-based detectors such as R-FCN or Faster R-CNN.
quote: DRBox is designed as a box-based method, whereas it is also possible to apply RBox into proposal based detection frameworks, e.g. R-FCN or Faster R-CNN.
realizationNote: Realized by OD042 (RoI Transformer) which integrated rotatable boxes into a proposal-based two-stage detector for oriented objects.

direction: Reuse the multi-scale local orientation information learned with RBox for other orientation-sensitive tasks.
quote: We are looking forward of this interesting property to be used in other orientation sensitive tasks.
realizationNote: RBox orientation information was not reused in other orientation-sensitive tasks in the corpus.

direction: Understand what the relation module learns when stacked, which the authors leave as future work.
quote: our understanding of how relation module works is preliminary and left as future work.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper explained what stacked relation/attention modules learn.

direction: Extend the relation module beyond detection to instance segmentation, action recognition, captioning and VQA.
quote: We do not see any reason preventing it from finding broader applications in vision tasks, such as instance segmentation [35], action recognition [48], object relationship detection [33]
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD057 (DETR) and OD072 (QueryInst) which carried attention/relation-style modelling into segmentation, while action recognition, captioning and VQA remained outside the corpus.

direction: Advance detection by modelling and understanding the various concurring factors (recognition, localization, quality matching).
quote: The solid and consistent detection improvements of the Cascade R-CNN on the challenging COCO dataset suggest the modeling and understanding of various concurring factors are required to advance object detection.
realizationNote: Realized by OD048 (Double-Head) which explicitly analyzed classification vs localization and OD054 (ATSS) which modeled label assignment, advancing detection through factor-level understanding.

direction: Apply the cascade architecture to other object detection research efforts and architectures.
quote: We believe that it can be useful to many future object detection research efforts.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper transplanted the cascade architecture into another detector family.

direction: Combine the fusion module with stronger backbones such as ResNet and DenseNet for better COCO performance.
quote: In the future, it is worth enhancing our FSSD with much stronger backbone networks such as ResNet [12] and DenseNet [13] to get better performance on the MSCOCO dataset
realizationNote: Realized by OD039 (M2Det) and OD053 (EfficientDet) which paired multi-scale feature-fusion detectors with ResNet-class and scaled backbones on COCO.

direction: Replace FPN inside Mask R-CNN with the proposed feature fusion module.
quote: replacing the FPN in Mask RCNN [10] with our feature fusion module is also an interesting research field.
realizationNote: Realized by OD033 (PANet) which replaced/augmented FPN inside Mask R-CNN with bottom-up path augmentation and adaptive feature pooling.

direction: Study the separation of network expressiveness (encoded by expansion layers) from capacity (encoded by bottleneck inputs) as a design axis.
quote: Exploring this is an important direction for future research.
realizationNote: The expressiveness-vs-capacity separation of bottleneck blocks was never studied as a design axis in the corpus.

direction: Investigate ReLU invertibility conditions further to gain insights useful for network design.
quote: We believe further study of this is warranted and might lead to helpful insights on network design.
realizationNote: ReLU invertibility conditions were not investigated further for network design in any later corpus paper.

direction: Apply the extension module to other computer vision tasks such as semantic segmentation.
quote: For future work we hope to apply this extension module to other computer vision tasks such as semantic segmentation.
realizationNote: ESSD's extension module was not applied to semantic segmentation or other vision tasks.

direction: Borrow ideas from super-resolution to improve object detection.
quote: We are going to borrow some ideas from super-resolution to improve objection detection.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper borrowed super-resolution ideas into detection.

direction: Use Generative Adversarial Networks to improve detection results.
quote: We also plan to use more advanced technologies such as Generative Adversarial Networks to improve our detection results.
realizationNote: GAN-based detection improvements were not pursued in any later corpus paper.

direction: Extend PANet from images to video and RGBD data.
quote: Our future work will be to extend our method to video and RGBD data.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD086 (streaming perception) which extended real-time detection to video, while RGBD data was never addressed.

direction: Investigate why medium/large object performance lagged despite strong APS.
quote: More investigation is needed to get to the bottom of this.
realizationNote: The YOLOv3 medium/large-object gap was not explained by any later corpus work.

direction: Revisit the rejected training techniques with tuning to stabilize training.
quote: It is possible that some of these techniques could eventually produce good results, perhaps they just need some tuning to stabilize the training.
realizationNote: Realized by OD056 (YOLOv4) and OD061 (PP-YOLO) which systematically re-tuned and stabilized rejected training techniques into a bag-of-freebies.

direction: Develop evaluation metrics that reflect what practitioners actually care about.
quote: if we’re going to come up with new metrics we should focus on these discrepancies
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD086 which introduced latency-aware streaming-perception evaluation, though practitioner-oriented metrics were not generally developed.

direction: Explore MetaAnchor on transfer tasks, where it shows potential under shifted box distributions.
quote: which shows the potential on the transfer tasks.
realizationNote: MetaAnchor was not explored on transfer tasks with shifted box distributions in the corpus.

direction: Further evaluate whether generated anchors can bridge the box-distribution gap between datasets.
quote: So, for MetaAnchor it is interesting to evaluate whether it is able to bridge the distribution gap between two dataset.
realizationNote: Generated anchors were never evaluated for bridging the box-distribution gap between datasets.

direction: Improve both corner detection and corner grouping, which the error analysis identifies as leaving ample room for improvement.
quote: there is still ample room for improvement in both detecting and grouping corners, the main bottleneck is detecting corners.
realizationNote: Realized by OD050 (CenterNet) which added a center keypoint to improve corner grouping and OD055 (CentripetalNet) which refined corner pairing.

direction: Use the interpretable predicted localization uncertainty in downstream applications such as self-driving cars and robotics.
quote: it can potentially be helpful in down-stream applications like self-driving cars and robotics [7, 16, 21].
realizationNote: Realized by OD047 (Gaussian YOLOv3) which exploited predicted localization uncertainty in an autonomous-driving camera detector.

direction: Evaluate ScratchDet with larger input image sizes than 300 x 300, which the authors expect to raise accuracy further.
quote: we believe that the accuracy of ScratchDet can be further improved using larger input size.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD053 and OD071 which confirmed that larger input sizes improve accuracy, though ScratchDet's own high-resolution runs were never reported.

direction: Prefer collecting and training on target-task data over ever-larger generic pre-training sets as compute and data grow.
quote: looking forward, when the community will proceed with more data and faster computation, our study suggests that collecting data and training on the target tasks is a solution worth considering
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD111 (DINO-X) which pre-trained on a large target-task grounding set rather than classification data, though ever-larger generic pre-training remained dominant.

direction: Shift data-collection effort into the target domain if classification-level pre-training gains keep diminishing.
quote: If the gain of large-scale classification-level pre-training becomes exponentially diminishing [44, 30], it would be more effective to collect data in the target domain.
realizationNote: Realized by OD081 (GLIP) and OD111 (DINO-X) which shifted collection and pre-training into the target detection/grounding domain at scale.

direction: Re-evaluate self-supervised and other pre-trained features against random-initialization baselines.
quote: our study suggests that the community should be more careful when evaluating pre-trained features
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD097 (Revisiting DETR Pre-training) which re-benchmarked self-supervised DETR pre-training against from-scratch baselines.

direction: Combine scale selection (SNIP-style) and cascade techniques with Grid R-CNN for further gains.
quote: we will try to combine the scale selection and cascade techniques with Grid R-CNN and we believe a further gain can be obtained.
realizationNote: Grid R-CNN was never combined with scale selection and cascade techniques in any later corpus paper.

direction: Design circle-shaped point layouts to better localize round objects.
quote: we are inspired to design points in circle shapes for better localization of objects with a round shape in future works.
realizationNote: Circle-shaped point layouts for round objects were not designed in the corpus.

direction: Exploit the anchor sparsity for faster inference by pairing it with a heavier detection head than the current single-convolution RPN head.
quote: Nevertheless, a significant reduction in the number of anchors offers a possibility to perform more efficient inference with a heavier head.
realizationNote: Realized by OD066 (Sparse R-CNN) which replaced dense anchors with a fixed sparse set of learnable proposals and a much heavier dynamic head for efficient end-to-end inference.

direction: Tune the inherited hyper-parameters specifically for FCOS, which the authors expect to improve results further.
quote: We hypothesize that the performance of our detector may be improved further if we carefully tune the hyper-parameters.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD059 (PAA) and OD062 (VarifocalNet) which improved FCOS-line performance through better assignment and losses, though explicit hyper-parameter tuning was not documented.

direction: Extend the anchor-free per-pixel framework to other instance-level recognition tasks such as instance segmentation and keypoint detection.
quote: We also believe that FCOS can be extended to solve many other instancelevel recognition tasks.
realizationNote: Realized by OD049 (CenterNet) which extended per-pixel focal-loss-style detection to keypoints/pose, 3D detection and segmentation in one framework.

direction: Deploy the improved camera-based detection system to broaden the use of autonomous driving applications.
quote: the proposed algorithm can significantly improve the camera-based object detection system for autonomous driving, and is consequently expected to contribute significantly to the wide use of autonomous driving applications.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper deployed or extended the Gaussian YOLOv3 camera-based autonomous-driving system.

direction: Share the analysis findings (head preferences for classification vs localization) with the broader object detection community as a basis for future research.
quote: We hope that our findings are helpful for future research in object detection.
realizationNote: Realized by OD075 (YOLOX) and OD091 (YOLOv6) whose decoupled classification/localization heads embody the head-preference finding reported here.

direction: Generalize the point-based representation beyond 2D detection to other recognition tasks.
quote: The idea is general and has broad applications beyond simple two-dimensional detection.
realizationNote: No later corpus paper generalized the point-based (center-point) representation beyond what CenterNet already covered in 2D detection.

direction: Develop real-time object recognition and related tasks along this line of work.
quote: Our initial experiments are encouraging and open up a new direction for real-time object recognition and related tasks.
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD075 (YOLOX) and OD086 (streaming) which brought anchor-free real-time detection to high speed, though the CenterNet line itself was not continued.

direction: Generalize the extra center-keypoint branch to other one-stage detectors such as SSD.
quote: We believe that our idea of adding an extra branch for the center keypoint can be potentially generalized to other existing one-stage approaches (e.g., SSD [27]).
realizationNote: Partially realized by OD055 (CentripetalNet) which extended center-point refinement in a one-stage keypoint detector, though not added onto SSD.

direction: Adopt advanced training strategies to improve performance.
quote: Meanwhile, some advanced training strategies [46] can be used for better performance. We leave as our future work.
realizationNote: Realized by OD056 (YOLOv4) and OD075 (YOLOX) which adopted advanced training strategies, including bag-of-freebies and stronger augmentation, to lift accuracy.

direction: Extend the EfficientDet/BiFPN design beyond detection to dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation.
quote: These results suggest that EfficientDet is also quite promising for semantic segmentation.
realizationNote: The BiFPN/EfficientDet design was never extended to semantic segmentation in the corpus.

direction: Re-examine what role tiling multiple anchors per location actually plays once positives are selected adaptively.
quote: it needs further study to discover its right role.
